command.mac:
cd ~
gh auth switch -u shivinate7
gh variable set TEAM_ID --repo shivinate7/mailaudit --body "$(plutil -extract team_id raw ~/.config/ios-ship/account.json)"
gh variable list --repo shivinate7/mailaudit
command.powershell:
cd ~
gh auth switch -u shivinate7
$t = (Get-Content "$HOME\.config\ios-ship\account.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).team_id
gh variable set TEAM_ID --repo shivinate7/mailaudit --body $t
gh variable list --repo shivinate7/mailaudit

context:
The Apple signing team id goes in a repo variable, never in the public repo (decision native-ships-via-testflight: tools/ios-ship.json holds no ID). The workflow .github/workflows/testflight.yml reads TEAM_ID; without it every upload stops at "TEAM_ID is unset".
Why yours: the team id lives only in the ios-ship account file on your Mac, and this session cannot read it (measured 2026-11-08, no TEAM_ID in env and no account.json under $HOME/.config/ios-ship in the cloud container).
holds: The first TestFlight upload from CI. Review of the lane goes on meanwhile.
